messages.subject: ez and Matlab
parts:
Hi Mike - This is a very helpful package, and this may not be the
appropriate place to ask this question, but I am having a strange
outcome using ez and matlab. Specifically, I am getting different F
values for some within subject interactions when I run ezANOVA using
the matlab code of evalR compared to when I run the ezANOVA from
within R. Specifically, I am getting correct F & p values for side &
phase, but incorrect values for the factor time. I'm running a mixed
anova (1 between subject (Side), 2 within (phase, time), with time
nested within phase. I get identical results with SPSS when I run
this solely within R, but not when I use the exact same commands sent
from matlab

e.g.,
evalR('data2 <- data.frame(effect = dv, subj = factor(subj1), side =
factor(gr1), phasefac = factor(phase), timefac = factor(time),
row.names = NULL)')
[RESULT, STATUS, MSG] = evalR('statout <- ezANOVA(data = data2, dv = .
(effect), wid = .(subj), within = .(phasefac,timefac), between = .
(side), type=3)',0)

If you have any thought or could help if I sent the data and the
script, please let me know.
thanks
matt

messages.author: a35295e56a3dac9c
messages.subject: Re: ez and Matlab
parts:
Forget it...I figured out the problem. For anyone else having
difficulty, you need to call the source files with the "Eval(...,0)"
option. maybe also the other commands.

e.g.,
[result,status,msg] = evalR('setwd("C:/R")',0);
[result,status,msg] = evalR('library(ez)',0);
[result,status,msg] = evalR('source("ezANOVA.R")',0);
[result,status,msg] = evalR('source("ez-internal.R")',0);
[result,status,msg] =
evalR('options(contrasts=c("contr.sum","contr.poly"))',0);
